metaDescription: Seven drill bit sharpeners compared on size range, point angle, split point, wheel type and learning curve, with picks for a home garage and a busy shop.
expertTake: The Drill Doctor 750X is our top pick for its wide size range and accurate chuck guided alignment. The Drill Doctor 350X is the value pick for common bits from 3/32 to 1/2 inch. Anyone who only owns small, inexpensive bits should skip a sharpener, since a new bit costs less than the time spent on restoring an old one.
introParagraphs: A bit sharpener grinds the cutting tip of a worn twist bit back to its original shape. A sharp bit cuts cleanly, runs cooler and needs less push, while a dull one burns, walks across the surface and makes oversized holes.

Sharpeners range from precision machines with chuck guides to bench grinder jigs. The right one depends on how many bits you own and how large they are. This guide compares seven options and explains what point geometry and wheel choices mean for you.

products.name: Drill Doctor 750X drill bit sharpener with Work Sharp pocket knife sharpener

specList.label: Bit types
specList.value: High speed steel, masonry, carbide with diamond wheel

products.description:
The Drill Doctor 750X is the flagship of the line, handling bits from 3/32 to 3/4 inch with a guided alignment system that sets the point and relief angles for you. The listing sells it with a Work Sharp pocket knife sharpener as a bonus.

The larger range matters because bits over 1/2 inch are the ones that cost real money and are worth restoring. The machine can create split points, which help a bit start without walking on metal, and it accepts a diamond wheel for carbide. Compared with the 500X, it covers bigger bits, and compared with the 350X, it offers more point choices. Compared with the VEVOR machines, it has a more guided process that new users learn faster.

Ownership comes down to wheel life and technique. Use light passes, keep the bit cool and replace the wheel when it glazes. Practice on cheap bits first, and expect a learning curve of an hour or two.
products.bestFor: Serious DIYers and small shops that sharpen bits over 1/2 inch.
pros: Handles bits from 3/32 to 3/4 inch
Chuck guided alignment sets angles accurately
Split point sharpening helps on metal
Includes a bonus knife sharpener
cons: Highest cost tier among the sharpeners here

products.name: Drill Doctor 500X drill bit sharpener with 118 and 135 degree point angles
products.description:
The Drill Doctor 500X handles bits from 3/32 to 1/2 inch and offers two point angles: 118 degrees for general work and soft materials, and 135 degrees for harder steel. A split point option creates a small chisel at the tip that stops the bit from wandering.

Choosing the point angle is the feature that sets it above the 350X. A 135 degree split point starts cleanly on stainless and hard metal, while 118 degrees suits wood and soft metals. Compared with the 750X, it covers fewer bit sizes but costs less. Compared with the VEVOR, it is a guided system, which means you learn faster but have less ability to customize angles.

Ownership is simple. Seat the bit in the chuck guide, use light passes, and replace the wheel when it wears. Plan to practice on scrap bits first.
products.bestFor: Metalworkers and builders who want 135 degree split point bits.
pros: Two point angles cover soft and hard materials
Split point sharpening prevents walking
Chuck guide makes alignment repeatable
Covers the most common 3/32 to 1/2 inch bits
cons: Does not handle bits over 1/2 inch

products.name: Drill Doctor 350X electric drill bit sharpener, 3/32 to 1/2 inch

specList.label: Bit types
specList.value: Steel, masonry and carbide per the listing

products.description:
The Drill Doctor 350X sharpens bits from 3/32 to 1/2 inch with a simple chuck based alignment system. It restores twist and masonry bits, and it offers a lower cost way into guided sharpening than the 500X or 750X.

It lacks the point angle choice and split point ability of the 500X, so it suits household bits used on wood, plastic and soft metal. Compared with the 500X, it is easier to learn because there are fewer options. Compared with the manual TECHPLUS jig, it gives repeatable results with much less skill.

Ownership centers on practice and wheel care. Sharpen a few old bits first, use light passes to avoid overheating and replace the wheel when it glazes. A bit that turns blue has been overheated and should be retired.
products.bestFor: Home users who want guided sharpening for common bit sizes.
pros: Guided alignment makes sharpening repeatable
Covers the common 3/32 to 1/2 inch range
Simpler than higher models, so easier to learn
Compact enough for a small bench
cons: No selectable point angles or split point
Limited to bits up to 1/2 inch

products.name: ANGLE BEAST 750X electric drill bit sharpener, 3/32 to 3/4 inch, 115 to 140 degrees

specList.label: Claim
specList.value: OEM comparable quality, per the maker

products.description:
The ANGLE BEAST 750X covers the same 3/32 to 3/4 inch range as the Drill Doctor 750X and offers adjustable point angles from 115 to 140 degrees. A practice drill bit is included, which is a useful touch for learning.

The maker claims OEM comparable quality, a phrase with no standard meaning that we treat as marketing. The wider angle range gives more control than the fixed choices on the Drill Doctor 500X. Compared with the Drill Doctor 750X, it costs less but has a shorter track record and less brand support. Compared with the VEVOR, it is a guided chuck style machine.

Ownership requires attention to the first few bits. Use the included practice bit, check the point symmetry and replace the wheel when it wears. If lips come out uneven, reseat the bit and try again.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a wide size range and angle adjustment at a lower cost.
pros: Handles bits up to 3/4 inch
Adjustable 115 to 140 degree point angle
Practice bit helps beginners learn
Costs less than the Drill Doctor 750X
cons: Shorter track record than Drill Doctor

products.name: VEVOR MR-13A+ drill bit sharpener, 3 to 15 mm, 5800 RPM, 13 collets, CBN wheel
products.description:
The VEVOR MR-13A+ is a precision grinding machine for 3 to 15 mm bits, using 13 collets to hold each size, a CBN grinding wheel and a 5800 RPM motor. The point angle adjusts from 95 to 135 degrees.

CBN, or cubic boron nitride, cuts high speed steel and cobalt cleanly and lasts longer than a standard wheel, which lowers the long run cost. The collet system holds each bit size exactly, which gives accurate lips, though it takes time to change collets. Compared with the Drill Doctor models, it offers more angle control but a steeper learning curve and fewer instructions. Compared with the MR-13B, it has the CBN wheel and more included collets.

Ownership is about setup. Choose the right collet, set the angle and relief, and make light passes. Check the lips with a magnifier and keep the machine clean of metal dust.
products.bestFor: Shops that sharpen many bits and want a CBN wheel and fine angle control.
pros: CBN wheel cuts HSS cleanly and lasts long
Thirteen collets hold each size exactly
Adjustable 95 to 135 degree point angle
Covers 3 to 15 mm bits
cons: Steeper learning curve than guided Drill Doctors

products.name: VEVOR MR-13B drill bit sharpener, 3 to 13 mm, two grinding wheels, 95 to 135 degrees

specList.label: Wheels
specList.value: Two grinding wheels to choose from

products.description:
The VEVOR MR-13B covers 3 to 13 mm bits with a 95 to 135 degree adjustable point angle and two replaceable grinding wheels. The maker also describes a lip relief setting with positioning pins that lets you customize the cutting geometry.

It is the lowest cost machine in the lineup, which makes it a sensible entry into precision grinding for users willing to learn. Compared with the MR-13A+, it has a narrower size range and a more basic wheel set. Compared with the Drill Doctor 350X, it has far more angle control but fewer helpers for beginners.

Ownership requires careful setup. Read the instructions, practice on a few cheap bits and check lip symmetry. Replace the wheels when they wear and keep the collet seat clean.
products.bestFor: Cost conscious users who want adjustable angles and are willing to learn.
pros: Lowest cost precision grinder in this lineup
Adjustable point angle from 95 to 135 degrees
Two wheels for different materials
Lip relief can be customized
cons: Instructions and support are thinner than Drill Doctor

products.name: TECHPLUS 3 set drill bit sharpener guide jig for bench grinders
products.description:
The TECHPLUS is a set of three 3D printed guide jigs that help you hold a bit against a bench grinder at a set angle. It offers several point angles, including 90 and 118 degrees, and it is the cheapest approach in this lineup.

The jig only guides your hands. You still need a bench grinder, steady control and a feel for how the lips should look, so the learning curve is steeper than with any machine here. Compared with the Drill Doctors, it will not produce a split point or a precise relief angle. For occasional sharpening of larger bits, it can be a workable low cost option if you already own a grinder.

Ownership is about technique. Cool the bit in water between passes, keep the lips even and check the point angle against a gauge. Plastic jigs wear, so keep spares.
products.bestFor: Bench grinder owners who sharpen a few larger bits on a budget.
pros: Lowest cost way to sharpen bits
Three jigs give a spare for wear
Several preset angles help consistency
Works with an existing bench grinder
cons: Needs a bench grinder and steady hands
Cannot create split points or accurate relief

buyingCriteria.explanation: Sharpeners list the minimum and maximum bit diameter they hold. Most household bits fall between 1/8 and 1/2 inch, and larger bits cost more and are more worth restoring. Buyers often forget that big bits are out of range for the cheaper models. The Drill Doctor 350X and 500X stop at 1/2 inch while the 750X reaches 3/4 inch.

A 118 degree point suits wood and soft metals, and 135 degrees with a split point suits harder steel and starts without walking. Adjustable machines let you choose. Fixed angle machines suit general work. The Drill Doctor 500X offers both angles, and the VEVOR machines adjust from 95 to 135 degrees.

Guided machines like the Drill Doctor set the angles for you and are easy to learn. Collet based machines like the VEVOR give more control but take longer to master. Beginners usually do better with guided systems. The Drill Doctor line is guided, and the VEVOR is collet based.

CBN wheels cut high speed steel and cobalt cleanly and last long, while diamond wheels are used for carbide, and standard abrasives wear faster. Replacement wheels are a running cost. Check wheel availability before buying. The VEVOR MR-13A+ includes a CBN wheel.

Overheating turns the bit blue and softens the steel. Use light passes, let the bit cool and avoid pushing hard. Technique matters as much as the machine. A practice bit helps. The ANGLE BEAST includes one.

A cheap small bit costs less than the time to sharpen it. Larger, cobalt and carbide bits are worth restoring. Count how many bits you own and how often you drill metal. A sharpener pays for itself with a collection of bits over 1/4 inch.

specDecoder.meaning: The angle at the tip where the two cutting lips meet. 118 degrees is standard, 135 degrees suits hard metals.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Drill Doctor 500X offers both, and the VEVOR lists 95 to 135.

specDecoder.meaning: A small notch cut into the chisel edge at the tip, which stops the bit from walking on metal.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Drill Doctor 500X and 750X can create one.

specDecoder.meaning: A grinding wheel coated with cubic boron nitride. It cuts steel cleanly and wears slowly.
A sleeve that grips a bit of a specific diameter. A set of collets covers a size range.
The angle behind the cutting lip that lets it bite. Too little rubs, too much weakens the edge.
specDecoder.watchFor: The VEVOR MR-13B lists adjustable relief, while the Drill Doctors set it automatically.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spec sheet review
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated size range, point angles, wheel type and alignment method from each listing. We compared them with what home and shop users need. The Drill Doctor 750X and VEVOR MR-13A+ anchored the comparison.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for repeating comments on uneven lips, wheel wear, learning curve and bit slipping. These issues decide whether a sharpener restores bits well. Uneven lips from a poor setup came up most.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit for the bits you own
howWeEvaluated.description: Small household bits, large metal bits and carbide bits need different machines. We graded each product on those cases.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cost relative to the lineup
howWeEvaluated.description: We used relative cost tiers and quote no listing prices. The TECHPLUS jig and VEVOR MR-13B sit at the low end, while the Drill Doctor 750X sits at the top.

howWeEvaluated.title: Claims we discounted
howWeEvaluated.description: Phrases like OEM comparable and professional grade appear often. We treat them as marketing and rank on size range, angle control and wheel type.

cards.text: A guided machine that covers 3/32 to 1/2 inch, with replaceable wheels and clear instructions. Practice on old bits first.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Drill Doctor 350X is the practical choice, with the 500X if you drill steel often.

maintenance.why: A worn wheel cuts slowly and overheats bits. A fresh wheel restores clean cutting.

maintenance.task: Clean metal dust from the machine
maintenance.why: Dust jams collets and chucks and affects alignment. A brush and compressed air keep it clear.
Setup errors give uneven lips that ruin good bits. Scrap bits protect your investment.
Uneven lips cause wandering and oversized holes. A quick look catches errors.
Missing collets make a machine less useful. A small case keeps them organized.

faq.q: Is it worth sharpening drill bits?
faq.a: For bits over 1/4 inch, cobalt or carbide bits, yes. A cheap small bit often costs less than the time to restore it.

faq.q: What point angle should I use?
faq.a: 118 degrees suits wood and soft metals, and 135 degrees with a split point suits harder steel. The Drill Doctor 500X offers both.

faq.q: Why did my sharpened bit wander?
faq.a: Uneven lips or a poor point symmetry usually cause it. Reseat the bit, make light passes and check the lips with a magnifier.
Yes, with a diamond wheel. Standard wheels do not cut carbide. Check that your machine accepts one.

faq.q: What does a blue bit mean?
faq.a: It has been overheated, which softens the steel. Use light passes and cool the bit, and retire a blued bit.
Guided machines are easier to learn and repeat. Manual jigs cost less but demand steady hands and a bench grinder.
